chunks: And 'Ad and Pharaoh and the brethren of Lot,

key_terms.إِخْوَانُ لُوطٍ: The brethren or people of Lot, referring to the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrah.
key_terms.عَادٌ: The tribe of 'Ad, an ancient Arab people known for their strength and eventual destruction.
key_terms.فِرْعَوْنُ: Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler of Egypt during the time of Prophet Moses.

ai.seo_question: Who are the people of 'Ad, Pharaoh, and the brethren of Lot mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this triad represents the archetypes of arrogance and rejection, with Pharaoh symbolizing political tyranny, 'Ad representing tribal pride, and the people of Lot illustrating moral corruption. Their collective mention underscores the inevitability of divine retribution against those who deny the prophetic mission, a theme central to the Surah's warning to the Quraysh.
